abstract: Reprogramming of endogenous Muller glia (MG) into functional neurons represents a promising therapeutic strategy for the treatment of irreversible retinal blinding diseases. In adult mammals, however, insufficient MG proliferation constitutes a primary bottleneck that restricts successful MG reprogramming and impairs retinal structural and functional restoration. Here, we demonstrated that simultaneous chemical inhibition of Hippo signaling with TRULI and activation of Wnt signaling with CHIR-99021 elicited robust proliferation of endogenous MG in the adult mouse retinal explants. Following combinatorial drug treatment, MG exhibited gradual induction of the retinal progenitor marker PAX6 and the bipolar/photoreceptor lineage determinant Otx2, without concomitant elevation of the fibrotic marker GFAP, supporting the initiation of MG reprogramming. Mechanistically, our findings revealed that YAP and {beta}-catenin might act cooperatively to induce the expression of MYC, a core transcription factor governing cell cycle progression and somatic cell reprogramming. Elevated MYC accumulation in MG transcriptionally activated Cyclin D1 expression, which, together with the downregulation of the cell cycle inhibitor p27Kip1, drove efficient MG cell cycle re-entry and proliferation. Collectively, this study establishes a pure chemical combinatorial strategy to trigger robust proliferation and initiate reprogramming of adult mammalian MG. Our findings provide a feasible alternative approach to promote retinal regeneration and lay a foundation for the future clinical treatment of degenerative retinal diseases.
